title: Muhammara with Roasted Red Peppers, Walnuts and Pomegranate Molasses
summary: Grilled, peeled red peppers are blended with toasted walnuts, panko, spring onions, pomegranate molasses, lemon and spices, then finished with a well of oil, molasses and crumbled walnuts.

ingredients.item: Aleppo pepper or mild chilli flakes
fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Roast the peppers
steps.text: Grill the peppers close to a hot grill for 15-20 minutes, turning every 5 minutes, until blackened and soft. Cover in a bowl for 15 minutes to steam.

steps.title: Toast the walnuts
steps.text: Toast the walnuts in a dry pan over medium heat for 4-5 minutes until fragrant. Cool.

steps.title: Peel
steps.text: Peel and seed the peppers, discard the stems and juices, and pat dry.

steps.title: Blend
steps.text: Blend the peppers, all but 3 walnut halves, the panko, spring onions, 2 tbsp molasses, lemon, cumin, paprika, half the Aleppo pepper, the salt and 3 tbsp oil to a coarse, thick purée.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Spread in a bowl, make a well and fill with the remaining oil, 1 tsp molasses and the rest of the Aleppo pepper. Crumble the reserved walnuts on top.

tips: Pat the peppers dry so the dip stays thick.
Pulse rather than blend smooth: muhammara should have some texture.
Pomegranate molasses varies in sharpness; add the last spoonful to taste.
storage: Keep covered in the fridge for up to 4 days. Do not leave out for more than 2 hours. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
